ph_portable_cassette_player.name: Smuggler's Cassette Player
ph_portable_cassette_player.description: A portable cassette player worn by time. The tape inside has no label, just a handwritten date. A reminder of when crossing Tarkov called for less silence.

ph_classic_laptop.name: Archivist's Laptop
ph_classic_laptop.description: An old laptop with inventory stickers on its lid and worn keys. It may once have held records from a Tarkov company. Its value now lies in what survived.

ph_circuit_board.name: Experimental Motherboard
ph_circuit_board.description: A circuit board with unusual components and traces of hand modifications. It looks like it came from a test bench rather than a production line.

ph_camera_01.name: Correspondent's Camera
ph_camera_01.description: A camera that seems to have followed someone through the last days before the blockade. Its strap is worn, but the lens is intact. To a collector, some pictures are worth more than money.

ph_vintage_radio_transceiver.name: Operation Zero Transceiver
ph_vintage_radio_transceiver.description: A rugged transceiver with scratched selectors and traces of a removed identification plate. The name Operation Zero circulates among military scrap dealers. No two accounts agree.

ph_vintage_video_camera.name: Reconnaissance Camcorder
ph_vintage_video_camera.description: An old camcorder with transport wear on its casing. It might have recorded a factory, an escape route or just a holiday. Without the footage, all that remains is guesswork.

ph_retro_multimeter.name: Laboratory Multimeter
ph_retro_multimeter.description: A multimeter from another era, with a faded scale and worn probes. Its workshop may have closed, but someone still recognizes a well-kept piece.

ph_digital_wrist_watch.name: Operator's Digital Watch
ph_digital_wrist_watch.description: An understated digital watch marked by years of use. For those trapped in Tarkov, counting the minutes took on a different meaning.

ph_gamepad.name: Hideout Controller
ph_gamepad.description: A game controller with a coiled cable and worn buttons. Someone once spent a quiet evening holding it. That is the hard part to picture now.

ph_small_plastic_torch.name: Explorer's Flashlight
ph_small_plastic_torch.description: A simple flashlight with a scratched casing, looking as though it passed through many backpacks. A collectible reminder of corridors where nobody wanted to be left in the dark.

ph_vintage_binocular.name: Observer's Binoculars
ph_vintage_binocular.description: Old binoculars with worn coating and signs of minor repairs. Whoever carried them probably preferred watching from a distance. An understandable habit in Tarkov.

ph_old_gas_mask.name: Historical Gas Mask
ph_old_gas_mask.description: An old-pattern gas mask with aged rubber and parts of uncertain origin. Its value is historical. Trusting it with your breathing would be another matter.

ph_seadogs_compass.name: Navigator's Compass
ph_seadogs_compass.description: An old-cased compass with handling marks on the metal. In a sealed city, knowing where north lies does not always help you find a way out.

ph_vintage_pocket_watch.name: Colonel's Pocket Watch
ph_vintage_pocket_watch.description: An old pocket watch with small scratches on its case and a well-kept chain. Nobody knows who owned it, but traders have taken to calling it the Colonel's watch.

ph_vintage_lighter.name: Veteran's Lighter
ph_vintage_lighter.description: A metal lighter with worn corners. It passed through many pockets before reaching this place. Some buyers pay more for those marks than for a new one.

ph_stick_grenade.name: Inert Historical Grenade
ph_stick_grenade.description: A stick grenade preserved as a historical piece, with no combat function. Its shape draws attention, but collectors care about the era it came from.

ph_fish_knife.name: Fisherman's Collectible Knife
ph_fish_knife.description: A narrow knife with a plain handle, kept as a collectible. It seems to have known more boats and fish-cleaning benches than battlefields.

ph_binoculars.name: Field Binoculars
ph_binoculars.description: Field binoculars with a worn strap and an unassuming look. They may have watched a checkpoint or a path through the trees. Whoever looked through them left no notes.

ph_magnifying_glass_01.name: Investigator's Magnifying Glass
ph_magnifying_glass_01.description: A plain-framed magnifying glass marked by use. The sort of object that belonged on a desk piled with documents. In Tarkov, small details often hide large stories.

ph_brass_blowtorch.name: Antique Brass Blowtorch
ph_brass_blowtorch.description: A brass blowtorch with old stains and darkened metal. It has the look of a workshop that repaired things instead of throwing them away.

ph_industrial_microscope.name: Experimental Microscope
ph_industrial_microscope.description: A sturdy microscope with adjustable parts and signs of careful use. It may have come from a laboratory or an industrial inspection station. Its original building may no longer exist.

ph_vintage_spacecraft_instrument.name: Space Navigation Instrument
ph_vintage_spacecraft_instrument.description: A navigation instrument with an unusual dial and worn paint. Its association with space programs fuels rumors. Proving where it came from is another story.

ph_binder_notebook.name: Researcher's Notebook
ph_binder_notebook.description: A worn-covered notebook with loose pages and handling marks. Not everything a researcher wrote ended up on a computer. Sometimes the last record fits in a backpack.

ph_round_spectacles.name: Professor's Glasses
ph_round_spectacles.description: Round glasses with a thin frame and subtle wear. The name Professor came from traders, not an identification card. The person behind the lenses remains unknown.

ph_vintage_stapler.name: Archive Zero Stapler
ph_vintage_stapler.description: An old stapler with bright paint and the heft of another era. It outlasted the desks it helped organize. Papers disappear easily; metal tends to stay.

ph_modified_thermos.name: Expedition Thermos
ph_modified_thermos.description: A scuffed thermos made for long journeys. It seems to have mattered more to its former owner than its appearance suggests.

ph_ratchet_wrench.name: Precision Ratchet Wrench
ph_ratchet_wrench.description: A ratchet wrench with wear on its contact surfaces. It may have belonged to someone who could take a machine apart without leaving spare pieces behind.

ph_pliers.name: Technician's Pliers
ph_pliers.description: A plain pair of pliers with pressure marks on the jaws and worn handles. Among all the scrap, it still looks like something someone insisted on keeping.

ph_adjustable_wrench.name: Historical Adjustable Wrench
ph_adjustable_wrench.description: An old adjustable wrench with a darkened mechanism and metal polished by use. Nothing fancy, just a piece that moved from bench to bench for years.

ph_cross_pein_hammer.name: Workshop Zero Hammer
ph_cross_pein_hammer.description: A workshop hammer with a marked handle and a battered head. The name Workshop Zero seems to have appeared after the blockade. Whoever worked there left no sign on the door.
